titulo: The seed and the garden: why AI is cultivated
lead: Nobody writes, line by line, a model's ability to code or plan. The labs create the conditions and the abilities emerge. You do the same on a different scale: the model arrives ready-made, and what you cultivate is the environment around it.
objetivo: separate what the lab cultivates (the model) from what you cultivate (the agent) and explain the cycle that makes the agent improve.

aprende.t: Why the model is the seed and doesn't change with use
What you cultivate: the envelope around the model
The cycle that turns errors into a better agent
Where the garden metaphor breaks down

hero_alt: A seed germinating in the soil next to a computer chip.

secoes.sub: Each turn is a harvest cycle. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: Everything starts with a real process: qualifying leads, organizing the week, scheduling appointments. Without a defined process, there's nothing to evaluate later.
The agent is the model (fixed, from the lab) plus the environment you wrote: role, context, tools, rules, examples, and memory.
The agent runs the task with the environment as it stands at that moment. This is where most people stop: they use it, like it or don't, and start over.
What was delivered. It can look good and be wrong: fluent text isn't correct text.
Someone measures it: right, partial, or wrong, and why. Without evaluation, the agent repeats the same error with the same confidence.
The evaluation becomes a concrete change in the environment: a new rule, an example, a limit. In the file, not in the conversation.

secoes.volta: Better agent: the next run starts from an adjusted environment
secoes.legenda: Before, we programmed the behavior. Now, we program the process that produces the behavior.

rolagem_fim.titulo: What changes from one harvest cycle to the next
rolagem_fim.texto: It's not the model. It's what you noted about where it went wrong and what you adjusted in the environment. The first four steps make the agent work; evaluation and feedback make it improve.
rolagem_fim.curto: What improves isn't the seed. It's the garden.

secoes.sub: The point almost everyone mixes up.

texto: Training, weights, and scale happen at Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek. It costs billions and you don't take part.
The result is the seed: abilities that emerged from training, some expected, others that surprised even the people who trained it.
The model arrives ready-made, with its weights frozen. What you cultivate is everything around it: role, context, tools, rules, examples, memory, evaluation, and feedback.
That envelope is what turns the same model into either a confused intern or a reliable professional.

exemplo.texto: In use, the model doesn't learn on its own. When you say "my AI got better," what improved was the garden. And the garden is yours.

texto: With traditional software, you write the exact rules and get exactly what was specified; an error is a bug on a single line.
With cultivated AI, you write the conditions and watch what emerges, and an error calls for a different environment: more context, another example, a new rule.
You don't need to be better than the AI at the task. You need to know how to create the environment where it produces the right result.
The work shifts from doing to defining the role, giving context, setting limits, evaluating, and giving feedback. It's people management, applied to systems.

secoes.titulo: Video: why your AI repeats the same mistake
secoes.sub: Ten minutes with Nei on the whole concept, with chapters and captions.
Read this before you get too excited.

passos.titulo: It doesn't grow on its own
texto: A plant grows on its own; an agent doesn't. Without evaluation and feedback, it repeats the same mistake forever.
A plant doesn't invent fruit. An agent can produce a result that looks good and is wrong. That's why evaluation exists.
Bad context, a bad example, and a vague rule produce a bad agent. The model is the same as your competitor's; the garden is not.
"Giving feedback" here means editing the environment, not chatting until it "understands."

secoes.sub: Copy them and use them in the practice below.

blocos.conteudo:
What do you do differently today compared to last month, and why?
If you can't answer with examples, say so clearly.

secoes.sub: Start by measuring where you are.

exercicios.texto: Open the project diagnostic and answer the eight questions thinking about the AI you use most today.
exercicios.pronto: you wrote down your score, the place to start, and which kit the diagnostic recommended.

exercicios.texto: Think of something you've already explained to the AI three or more times (a format, a tone, a piece of data). Write it in a note: what you keep repeating and which of the eight elements it should live in (context, rule, or example).
exercicios.pronto: the note has the repeated correction and the element where it will live.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after you try.

perguntas.p: After a month of use, your AI makes fewer mistakes. What changed?
opcoes: The model's weights were adjusted by your conversations
The environment around the model: context, rules, examples, and memory
The lab released a new version just for you
perguntas.explica: In use, the weights stay frozen. What learns is the system: the files you write and review. The common mistake is thinking the model "learned from you."

perguntas.p: Which step of the cycle do most people skip?
perguntas.explica: Using it and starting over is the default. Without measuring the result and feeding the correction back into the environment, the cycle doesn't close and the agent doesn't improve.

perguntas.p: What does "giving feedback" mean in cultivation?
opcoes: Chatting with the AI until it understands
Editing the environment: a new rule, example, or limit
perguntas.explica: Feedback is a concrete change to the file. Repeating the explanation in the chat disappears in the next session.

perguntas.p: Two companies use the same model. Why are the results so different?
opcoes: One paid for a more expensive plan
The garden around the model is different
perguntas.explica: The model is available to everyone. The difference lies in the context, rules, examples, and evaluation that each company has built.

itens.texto: The lab cultivates the model; you cultivate the agent.
Process, agent, execution, result, evaluation, feedback, better agent.
Feedback is editing the environment, not repeating it in the chat.
